newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end mostly firm on soy gain.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end mostly firm on soy gain.

text.p: Gains in most soybean contracts, tied to concerns about dry weather and some outlooks for a cool front to move into the U.S. Midwest by the weekend, boosted CBOT soy product futures to a mostly higher close, traders said.
Dry conditions in the key U.S. soy growing region and possible cool weather would hamper soybeans during their critical pod filling stage of development, they said.

Meteorologists early Tuesday said most of the U.S. Midwest can expect highs in the 80s (degrees Farenheit) and little precipitation through Thursday but disagreed on prospects for much cooler weather next week.
Some frosty temperatures were forecast for portions of the Canadian Prairies by the weekend and there were some concerns the cold front may move into the U.S. Midwest.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, down from 19,945 Friday, according to the CBOT. Soymeal options volume was estimated at 900 contracts, down from 1,822 Friday.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 13,000 contracts, down from 25,322 Friday. Soyoil options volume was estimated at 400 contracts, up from 216 Friday.
Soymeal closed $1.30 per ton higher to $2.00 lower, with September up $0.70 at $267.40.
Soyoil futures closed 0.09 cent per lb higher to 90.01 lower, with September up 0.05 at 25.38 cents.
